notice: Draft plan as of Oct 1. The proposal goes to the professor next week, so groups and tasks may still change.

groups.name: Data and segments
groups.goal: Build one clean pipeline segment layer with stable IDs, distance rings and a reference ring.

tasks.what: Find out why 16,300 pipelines became 1.86 million polygons at 100 m
Give every pipeline segment one ID that stays the same at every distance
Build 0 to 100, 100 to 250 and 250 to 500 m rings, plus a 500 to 1,000 m reference ring
Audit last year's tables: rows, blanks and duplicates per ecoregion

groups.name: Earth Engine in Python
groups.goal: Turn last year's Earth Engine script into a documented Python program that runs every region and year.

tasks.what: Get everyone registered for Earth Engine and into one shared Cloud project
Port last year's script to the Python API and match its 250 m Deserts values
Fix the cloud mask, switch to NDWI from bands 8 and 11, and add pixel counts
Run March to May for 2019 to 2025 in a loop that exports to Drive

groups.name: Analysis and maps
groups.goal: Join the results, compare each ring with its reference, and make the GIS Day maps.

tasks.what: Write one Python join that reports matched, unmatched and blank rows
Add a soil class from gSSURGO or STATSGO2 to each ring
Compare each ring with its reference by ecoregion and pipe diameter
Make the GIS Day maps with one color scale for every distance

problems.name: Join IDs use a space instead of an underscore in one table
17% of rows have no NDVI or NDWI value
Combined tables are smaller than the tables they were built from
IDs differ between 100, 250 and 500 m, so distances cannot be compared
About 110 polygons per pipeline line at 100 m
Plains attribute table sits at the 2 GB shapefile limit
Simplify Polygon dropped features without a record
Second index is MNDWI, a water index, not NDWI for plant moisture
No pixel or image count behind each value
One season only, March to May 2025
No reference area to compare against
Map shows NDWI at 100 m but NDVI at 250 and 500 m
